help.title: Help
help.basicsBody:
Encrypt: Go to the Encrypt tab, choose the files or folders you want to encrypt (multiple selection is supported), enter a password, and press Encrypt.

Decrypt: Two ways — double-click the .locked marker file left at the original location, or find the item in the Encrypted Items tab and use its unlock button.

Encrypted Items: View all currently encrypted items, decrypt them individually, permanently delete them, and see the full activity history.
help.howItWorksBody:
After encryption, the content is moved to a centralized storage location (the Vault). Only a marker file named .locked is left at the original location — it contains no original content, and simply marks that something used to be there.

There are three independent unlock methods that can be enabled together: password (always required; the other two are optional extras), Passkey (quick unlock using this device's Windows Hello), and recovery key (a one-time-displayed backup code).

The Vault location can be changed in Settings to a cloud sync folder (e.g. OneDrive), letting multiple devices share the encrypted content through your sync client for cross-device backup — but the password itself is never synced; you need to remember it yourself.
help.precautionsBody:
Forgotten password = data cannot be recovered. This is by design — there is no backdoor, and no one, including the developer, can help restore it.

Passkey is bound to this specific device. It won't work on a different device — you'll need the password or recovery key there instead.

The recovery key is shown only once. Once you close that screen, it can never be shown again — be sure to copy, save, or write it down immediately.

"Permanently Delete" in the Encrypted Items list truly destroys the encrypted content — it does not just remove it from the list — and this action cannot be undone.
